vectors.desc: STRING "hi": fused token, inline length, raw bytes

token 62 = class 6 << 4 | inline length 2, then raw bytes 6869: byte length argument followed by that many raw bytes (WF-23 :703, :711; WF-13 :419-420)

vectors.desc: STRING FF FE: non-UTF-8 byte sequence is legal — no validity gate
deriv: envelope (c4 DD r5): root DESC E0 D8 0D — STRING, empty body (WF-22 :624)
header (WF-3 :194-198); token 62 + raw bytes FF FE (WF-23 :711)
FF FE is not valid UTF-8: any byte sequence is legal — a string is a byte sequence, not mandated text; the UTF-8 gates are binding projection content, not core (WF-13 :420-421)

vectors.desc: interned string repeat: first occurrence literal (id 0), second a REF token
deriv: envelope (c4 DD r5): root DESC E0 D8 0D — STRING kinds the stream (id 0); the literal behind it interns id 1; value 2 is the identity REF d1 (WF-22 :624; WF-24 :745-753)

value 1: token 62 + 6162 — the STRING literal registers intern id 1 (after the DESC, id 0); ids are ARG-encoded, DFS preorder from 0, interned strings share the one per-stream id space (WF-24 :745-753, :762-765)
value 2: repeat is a REF token D1 = class D << 4 | inline id 1; a repeated encounter MUST be a REF, duplicating a record body in one stream is forbidden (WF-23 :718; WF-24 :766-769; WF-13 :421-423)
envelope (c4 DD r5): root DESC E0 D8 09 — one BOOL descriptor types both values of the two-value stream; a type repeat carries no second body (WF-22 :623-625; WF-24 :766-769)
header (WF-3 :194-198); tokens 10 = selector 0 false, 11 = selector 1 true — class 1 << 4 | selector (WF-10 :379-380; WF-23 :703, :706)
envelope (c4 DD r5): root DESC E0 D8 09 (BOOL) — would-be canonical prefix before the reserved selector (WF-22 :623)
selector 2 of class 1: all selectors but 0/1 are reserved and a decoder MUST reject them (WF-10 :379-380; class bool_reserved_selector)

vectors.desc: BLOB L=4 E=2: dense prefix + implicit zero tail
deriv: envelope (c4 DD r5): root DESC E0 D8 0E — BLOB kind 14, empty body; the blob record registers behind it (id 1) (WF-22 :625)
header (WF-3 :194-198); token 74 = class 7 << 4 | inline L 4, ARG E = 02, then E raw bytes 5A 51 (WF-23 :703, :712; WF-14 :428-430)
bytes at [2,4) are implicit zeros — trailing-zero elision; byte at E−1 = 51 nonzero, E minimal (WF-14 :430-431)

vectors.desc: BLOB L=4 E=0: full elision, all-zero backing
deriv: envelope (c4 DD r5): root DESC E0 D8 0E — BLOB, empty body (WF-22 :625)
token 74 (inline L 4), ARG E = 0: empty dense prefix, all four backing bytes implicit zeros (WF-14 :429-430)
E minimality at E=0 is vacuous — the byte-at-E−1 rule bounds only a nonempty dense prefix; one legal spelling (WF-14 :430-431)
envelope (c4 DD r5): root DESC E0 D8 0E (BLOB) — would-be canonical prefix before the E/L violation (WF-22 :625)
token 72 (inline L 2), ARG E = 3: E MUST NOT exceed L — halt prefix at the E byte (WF-14 :430; class blob_E_gt_L)

vectors.desc: BLOB zero dense tail byte rejected: non-minimal E
deriv: envelope (c4 DD r5): root DESC E0 D8 0E (BLOB) — would-be canonical prefix (WF-22 :625)

L=4, E=2, dense bytes 5A 00: the byte at E−1 is zero — E is not minimal, a zero dense tail byte is non-canonical and a decoder reject (checked on materialized and skipped blobs alike) (WF-14 :430-433; class blob_zero_dense_tail)
